database_summary: This is a small clickstream / e-commerce style dataset stored in SQLite. It contains user master tables, many event/log tables (activity, access, action, read, form, error, purchase), product master snapshots (two dated tables), category master, and some app-specific user replicas and a card table. Event tables are timestamped and are the main facts; master tables are descriptive. Some tables contain overlapping columns (session, user_id, action) so joins are common but may multiply rows when joining event tables because they are at different granularities or contain duplicate sessions. Several tables appear to be historical/event streams rather than a single current state. No explicit foreign key constraints are defined in DDL, but column names imply relationships (user_id, product_id, session).

accepted.name: users_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_id,
  sex,
  birth_date,
  register_date,
  register_device,
  withdraw_date
FROM mst_users
accepted.description: Normalized user master rows with preserved identifiers and canonicalized date fields. Useful as the base user dimension for joins to event tables, cohorts, and retention analyses. | Use for: join users to events for per-user aggregates; filter active users by withdraw_date IS NULL; cohort by register_date or register_device

accepted.name: action_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  session,
  user_id,
  action,
  category,
  products,
  amount,
  stamp
FROM action_log
accepted.description: Canonicalized action events from action_log preserving session/user/action/time and product list. Use this as the cleaned action fact for downstream aggregates, product-explode CTEs, and join to users. | Use for: count actions by type/time/category; compute revenue by user or product after exploding products; session-level funnel analyses when joined to activity/read/form logs

accepted.name: action_events_with_ip
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.session,
  a.user_id,
  a.action,
  a.category,
  a.products,
  a.amount,
  a.stamp,
  ai.ip
FROM action_log a
LEFT JOIN action_log_with_ip ai
  ON a.session = ai.session
  AND a.user_id = ai.user_id
  AND a.stamp = ai.stamp
accepted.description: Denormalized action events augmented with IP where available by left-joining action_log to action_log_with_ip on session, user_id and stamp. Preserves all event rows from action_log and attaches ip if present. Useful for linking behavior to IP-level grouping or geolocation enrichment. | Use for: identify distinct IPs per user/session; filter suspicious activity by IP; aggregate revenue by IP or geolocation

accepted.name: activity_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  stamp,
  session,
  action,
  option,
  path,
  search_type
FROM activity_log
accepted.description: Normalized activity log events preserving session-level navigation details. Useful for page-path analysis, search behavior, and session funneling when joined to action/read/form logs. | Use for: session path/funnel analyses; counts of search_type or path usage; join to action_events to sequence actions and pageviews

accepted.name: purchase_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  purchase_id,
  user_id,
  amount,
  stamp
FROM purchase_log
accepted.description: Canonicalized purchase-level fact preserving purchase_id, user, amount and timestamp. Use for revenue and lifetime value calculations and join to users or products. | Use for: total revenue by user or period; LTV or cohort revenue analyses; join purchases to user attributes

accepted.name: product_master_latest
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  name,
  price,
  updated_at,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS product_rank
FROM (
  SELECT product_id, name, price, updated_at FROM mst_products_20161201
  UNION ALL
  SELECT product_id, name, price, updated_at FROM mst_products_20170101
)

semantic_filters.product_rank: use product_rank = 1 in downstream queries to select latest per product_id

accepted.description: Latest product master per product_id merged from available snapshot tables. Uses ROW_NUMBER() over updated_at to pick the most recent row per product_id. Useful to get current product attributes for joins to sales or action-exploded product ids. | Use for: get current price/name for a product_id; join product attributes to exploded product-level sales or action events

accepted.name: product_sales_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  category_name,
  SUM(sales) AS total_sales
FROM product_sales
GROUP BY product_id, category_name
accepted.description: Aggregated sales per product_id and category_name from product_sales. Useful for ranking products and joining to product master for attribute enrichment. | Use for: top selling products by category; trend comparisons when joined with snapshot master

accepted.name: session_event_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.session,
  COALESCE(a.action_count,0) AS action_count,
  COALESCE(act.activity_count,0) AS activity_count,
  COALESCE(r.read_count,0) AS read_count,
  COALESCE(f.form_count,0) AS form_count
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT session FROM (
    SELECT session FROM action_log
    UNION ALL
    SELECT session FROM activity_log
    UNION ALL
    SELECT session FROM read_log
    UNION ALL
    SELECT session FROM form_log
  )
) s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session, COUNT(*) AS action_count
  FROM action_log
  GROUP BY session
) a ON s.session = a.session
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session, COUNT(*) AS activity_count
  FROM activity_log
  GROUP BY session
) act ON s.session = act.session
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session, COUNT(*) AS read_count
  FROM read_log
  GROUP BY session
) r ON s.session = r.session
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT session, COUNT(*) AS form_count
  FROM form_log
  GROUP BY session
) f ON s.session = f.session
accepted.description: Per-session counts of different event types (action, activity, read, form) computed by left-aggregating each event table. Useful for session quality scoring, funnel definitions, and segmenting heavy sessions. | Use for: identify sessions with high engagement; correlate session activity with purchases when joined to purchases by session->user mapping

accepted.name: exploded_products
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  session,
  user_id,
  action,
  category,
  TRIM(value) AS product_id,
  amount,
  stamp
FROM action_log,
  (SELECT
     CASE
       WHEN value IS NULL OR value = '' THEN NULL
       ELSE value END AS value
   FROM (
     SELECT '' AS value
   )
  ) dummy
WHERE 1 = 1
-- The above dummy is a placeholder; SQLite lacks a built-in string-split. Downstream engines should replace this with an appropriate splitting method or use recursive CTEs.
accepted.description: Explode comma-separated products strings from action_log into one row per product within each action event. Preserves session/user/action/stamp and exposes product_id for joins to product masters or product-level sales. Useful for product-level funnels and revenue attribution. | Use for: product-level counts from action events; join actions to product master for pricing or naming

accepted.name: latest_product_attributes
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  name,
  price,
  updated_at
FROM product_master_latest
WHERE product_rank = 1

semantic_filters.product_rank: must be 1 to represent latest per product_id

accepted.description: Helper that selects only the latest product master rows by filtering product_master_latest where product_rank = 1. Useful to join current product attributes to sales or exploded product events. | Use for: get current product names/prices for product_id; enrich product-level actions or sales with attributes
